messages:
Alex: Quick check — during the Dedicated rollout yesterday, a tenant hit a per-route threshold and we saw alerts firing even though the console preview showed 'no notify'. Anyone know why the routing and the preview disagree?
Samira: Hmm, saw that. Which route+policy? Can you paste the preview screenshot or the route id? :eyes:
Alex: route_id: `svc-search.prod.v1`
Alex: screenshot: (attached) — preview panel shows 'notify: suppressed by quiet window', but alerts went to oncall.
Jon: Likely a mismatch between the preview logic (frontend) and the backend's evaluated routing at time-of-event. We changed quiet-window precedence last week. Frontend may be using cached policy.
Eva: I dug into the event — the alert's timestamp was 2025-09-02T14:12:23Z and the policy had a dynamic quiet-window that depends on tenant burn rate. Backend evaluated it as outside quiet window because burn rate had spiked right before.
Samira: So the preview is static snapshot, not computing tenant-level burn rate? That would explain.
Jon: Right — preview currently uses the stored policy config + last-known burn-rate bucket (stale up to 5m). Real-time evaluation uses the streaming telemetry which can flip buckets.
Alex: For UX we should surface 'preview as of' or show stale indicator. Users assume preview == live behavior.
Samira: Agreed. Also think about adding a tooltip: "Realtime factors (burn, quota) may change routing decisions".
Eva: Longer term, we should compute a quick-sim on the backend for the preview: run the same evaluation engine against a synthetic recent telemetry sample. That would reduce surprises.
Jon: Backend-sim sounds good but heavier. Could we keep a cheaper option: "preview with latest telemetry (best-effort)" vs "preview config-only" toggle?
Samira: That seems like a reasonable tradeoff. PM preference: default to config-only (fast) but show banner: "Preview ignores burst telemetry. Toggle to include recent telemetry".
Alex: Also request: when the console suggests suppression, include a short explanation: e.g., "Suppressed due to quiet-window: tenant burn 0.8 < threshold 0.9" or "Suppressed (stale telemetry)".
Jon: We can add a small delta check: if preview outcome != recent-eval outcome, surface a warning. Implementation: 1) endpoint `/api/preview-eval` that accepts route, policy, tenant-id; 2) backend runs eval against last-10s aggregated telemetry; 3) response includes `outcome`, `reasons[]`, `telemetry_age_s`.
Eva: Also add a log id in the preview panel so oncall can cross-ref the actual alert evaluation. That will speed triage.
Samira: Action items: Jon to prototype the `/api/preview-eval` toggle (POC in 2w), Eva to write a short playbook note about burn-rate edgecases in rollout, Alex to update UX mock with the toggle and stale banner.
Jon: One more thing — how do we want to handle rollouts? If we change quiet-window precedence, we need to rollout to backend and frontend in lockstep. Otherwise mismatch again. We should gate frontend changes on backend deploy completion.
Alex: Agreed. Maybe Console should call the backend capability endpoint before enabling toggle. `GET /capabilities` -> {"previewRealtime": true}.
Samira: I'll add gating to the rollout checklist. Also notify Support so they can expect increased tickets during the transition.
DeployBot: Canary started for eng-platform/frontend at commit `c3f4a2d` — traffic 5% to canary.
Eva: Ping me when backend canary is up so we can test preview-eval link.
Alex: Thanks all. Will file a small RFC summarizing UX change + API contract and link here. :thumbsup:
